prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: Across the five frames, the depth map traces the camera wearer moving from a doorway (~1–1.5 m ahead in frame 1) past a glass partition (~0.5–1 m in frame 2) into an office corridor (frame 3) before turning to face a person standing directly in front at ~0.5–0.8 m (frames 4–5). In frame 3, the map separates the foreground floor and bottom-edge objects (<0.5 m, bright white, within the camera wearer's arm's reach) from the central pillar (~2 m), a room divider (~3.5 m), and the distant corridor on the left (>6 m, nearly black), though the distant person on the far left is barely distinguishable from the dark background. In frames 4 and 5, the standing person's torso (facing the camera wearer, with their head cropped out above the top edge) forms a bright silhouette at ~0.5–0.8 m, with an even brighter coffee cup and paper bag at the bottom edge (~0.3–0.5 m, within arm's reach of both the camera wearer and the person) occluding the person's lower body, and a sofa with pillows ~2–3 m behind them to the left. The depth map makes the continuous 3D distance separation between the foreground objects, the close person, the vertical partition frame (~1.5 m), and the recessed sofa much clearer than the motion-blurred RGB frames. However, the depth map is unreliable on transparent and reflective glass surfaces—treating the glass window in frame 2 as a deep black void and flattening the glass wall in frames 3–5 into the room behind it—and blurs fine boundaries in frame 1.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates discrete foreground entities across the last three frames while leaving the doorway and motion-blurred glass in frames 1 and 2 completely unlabelled. In frame 3, it detects a distant person on the far left (~5–7 m away, partially occluded by the left frame edge) and misclassifies the right-side lounge area (~1.5–4 m away) as a 'tv' mask, while missing the architectural walls, partition, and furniture entirely. In frames 4 and 5, a large pink 'person' mask captures the torso and arms of the individual standing ~0.5–0.8 m directly in front of and facing the camera wearer (within arm's reach, with their head out of view above the frame and lower body cropped below), shifting from center to the right side of the frame as the camera wearer turns and approaches slightly. In frame 5, the white paper bag at the bottom left (~0.3–0.5 m away, within arm's reach of both people and touched by the person's right hand) is segmented as a separate purple mask occluding the lower edge of the person mask, though it is mislabelled as a 'book'. While segmentation sharply delineates the close person's silhouette and outstretched right arm from the cluttered background sofa (~2–3 m behind to the left) better than the dark RGB clothing, it is unreliable for scene layout, misses the coffee cup in frame 4, and produces detached false-positive 'person' fragments on the upper-left background in frames 4 and 5.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is completely blank for frames 1 through 4, providing no spatial information about the room layout, objects, the distant person in frame 3, or the close standing person in frame 4 despite their torso and hand being clearly visible ~0.6 m away in the RGB image. Only in frame 5 does a skeleton appear on the right side of the frame for the person standing ~0.4–0.8 m in front of the camera wearer, showing their torso facing toward the camera wearer and their right arm extending downward and to the left into arm's reach (~0.4 m) where a magenta hand skeleton grasps the paper bag at the bottom edge. This skeleton makes the exact joint articulation of the person's right arm and fingers on the bag explicit despite dark clothing and motion blur in the RGB image. However, the pose map is highly unreliable across the sequence: it fails to detect any keypoints in the first four frames, and in frame 5 the cropped head and occluded lower body cause the estimator to hallucinate a compressed vertical torso with two upward-pointing neck/head segments and folded lower-limb keypoints bunched at the bottom edge.
